title: Jim Owens: OU All-American End Turned Washington Coach
question: Which former Oklahoma All-American end later coached Washington to the Rose Bowl?
answer: Jim Owens, an end at Oklahoma from 1946 to 1949 and a 1949 first-team All-American, coached the University of Washington from 1957 to 1974 and led the Huskies to Rose Bowl wins after the 1959 and 1960 seasons.
summary: Jim Owens starred at end for Bud Wilkinson's Sooners (1946-49), then spent 18 seasons as Washington's head coach and led the Huskies to three Rose Bowls.
body: Jim Owens was an Oklahoma City kid who went to Classen High School and, after Navy Air Corps service interrupted his plans, arrived at OU for the 1946 season. He played four years in Norman, one under Jim Tatum and three under Bud Wilkinson. Wilkinson later called him one of the best tight ends to play college football.

The 1949 Sooners were the peak. Owens was a co-captain on a team that went 10-0 in the regular season, outscoring opponents 364 to 88, and he earned first-team All-America honors. Oklahoma then beat LSU 35-0 in the Sugar Bowl. In his last two seasons, the Sooners were 21-1.

Coaching came next. Owens learned under Bear Bryant at Texas A&M, and in 1957, at just 29, he took over a Washington program recovering from probation. He stayed 18 seasons, through 1974, and finished 99-82-6. He also served as Washington's athletic director from 1960 to 1969.

His Huskies reached the Rose Bowl three times, and the Hall of Fame notes that his 1959 and 1960 teams won there. In 2003 Washington put a bronze statue of him outside Husky Stadium. After leaving coaching he built a career as an oil executive.
Owens entered the College Football Hall of Fame in 1982 as a player, a fitting nod to his Sooner days. He died June 6, 2009, at his home in Bigfork, Montana, at age 82.
